title: FirstQuadrantTotalShortExact
statement: Let $C$ be an abelian category in which every double cochain complex indexed by $\mathbb N^2$ has its total complex for degree $p+q$ (the totalization used in [lem-sp-double-complex-vertical-tower-maps]). For every short exact short complex $S$ of such double complexes, applying totalization and then extension by zero from $\mathbb N$ to $\mathbb Z$ to its objects and maps gives a short exact short complex.

source.place: Finite-diagonal total complex construction and Lemma 12.25.3; complementary truncation comparison in Mathlib Algebra/Homology/Embedding/AreComplementary.lean, lines 306-328

proof.text: Evaluate S in each bidegree; evaluation preserves short exactness. For total degree n the set of pairs p+q=n is finite, including the single pair in degree zero. A finite biproduct of kernel sequences is a kernel sequence: lift each component through its kernel and use biproduct uniqueness. The summed first map is mono and the summed second map is epi, so the diagonal sequence is short exact. The coproduct-biproduct isomorphisms identify this sequence with the degree-n totalized short complex. Apply the degreewise short exactness criterion. Extension by zero has the same sequence in nonnegative degrees and a zero sequence in negative degrees; use extendXIso and the criterion again.

proof_origin.place: Finite-diagonal argument, specialized to canonical smart truncations; Lean assembly by N3
